biography.plain_text: Patrick E. Malloy III was an American property developer and investor who built his own real estate business after working in commodities. Based in Sag Harbor and Key Largo, he combined waterfront development with substantial petroleum and banking interests. He chaired Goodrich Petroleum and previously led the board of New York Bancorp.

long_biography.plain_text:
Patrick Malloy helped reshape Sag Harbor by finding new uses for its industrial waterfront. He restored a former Grumman aerospace plant as a mixed-use property that became home to Bay Street Theater. The theatre also counted him among its trustees. His marina businesses served the recreational boating trade that grew alongside the village’s resort economy.

Sport occupied an enduring place in his life. A Penn State business graduate and varsity lacrosse player, he twice captained a United States sailing team in international competition. He and his wife, Candace, later pledged $5 million to endow Penn State’s head football coaching position. The fund’s income was intended for needs including players’ academic support and medical care, recruiting and coaching expenses.
